name: Kettlebell Swing
summary: An explosive hip hinge that swings a kettlebell to chest height using hip power. It builds the glutes and hamstrings and conditioning. A dumbbell held by one end can replace the kettlebell.
setup: Place a kettlebell about a foot in front of you. A dumbbell held vertically by one end also works.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder width and toes slightly out.
Hinge your hips back, keep your back flat, and grab the handle with both hands.
Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, with the forearms against your thighs.
execution: Drive your hips forward explosively, squeezing your glutes, and let the kettlebell float up to chest height.
Keep your arms relaxed as hooks, since the hips make the weight move.
Stand tall at the top with ribs down and glutes tight.
Let the bell fall and hinge your hips back as it swings between your legs, then repeat.
mistakes: Squatting the swing: push the hips back and keep the shins nearly vertical.
Lifting with the arms and shoulders: let the hips power it and keep arms loose.
Leaning back at the top: finish with a tall, braced stance and ribs down.
Rounding the back at the bottom: keep the chest up and hinge from the hips, and use a lighter weight.
